ontology.purpose: Build a joint-level process ontology of Joint Intelligence Preparation of the Operational Environment (JIPOE) from JP 2-01.3, enabling a joint-planning support system to answer, for each JIPOE step, substep, product, and organizational role, what it is, what its purpose is, who performs it, what inputs it uses and outputs it produces, and how it supports joint operation planning, execution, and assessment. The ontology must also represent the analytic constructs JIPOE defines (operational environment dimensions, systems perspective/PMESII, adversary and relevant-actor models, courses of action, indicators) and their defining properties.
ontology.scope: IN SCOPE: JIPOE overview — definition, purpose, principles, and relationship to service IPB and the joint intelligence process; roles and responsibilities of joint staff elements and intelligence organizations; the four JIPOE steps — define the operational environment, describe its impact, evaluate the adversary and other relevant actors, determine their courses of action — with their substeps, products, and templates; JIPOE support to planning (JPP), execution, and assessment; special considerations for irregular warfare, countering asymmetric approaches, and domestic operations; the case-study appendix and glossary definitions. OUT OF SCOPE: service-specific IPB techniques covered only in ATP 2-01.3, collection management procedures, and specific adversary intelligence.
